title: Suggesting, accepting, declining
why: The lesson puts the future and the conditional to work in social life: suggesting an outing (¿Te apetece…? ¿Qué tal si…?), accepting, politely declining with an excuse, and setting up a meeting with quedar. It wraps up the unit "Plans and politeness" before moving on to comparisons and shopping.

{"lessons": ["

Making a suggestion

PhraseExampleTranslation
¿Te apetece + infinitive or noun?¿Te apetece ir al cine?Do you feel like going to the movies?
¿Qué tal si + present?¿Qué tal si cenamos fuera?How about we eat out?
¿Por qué no + present?¿Por qué no vamos a la playa?Why don't we go to the beach?
¿Vienes…? ¿Vamos…?¿Vienes a la fiesta de Marta?Are you coming to Marta's party?
¿Quedamos…?¿Quedamos el sábado?Shall we meet up on Saturday?

Apetecer: the \"feel like\" verb

Apetecer works like gustar: me apetece, te apetece, os apetece… and agrees with the thing you feel like: ¿Te apetece un café? / ¿Te apetecen unas tapas? It's the most Spanish way to suggest something. In Latin America, people tend to say ¿Tienes ganas de…? or ¿Quieres…?

The \"if\" trap: use the present!

In English, you might suggest with a past tense: \"What if we went to the movies?\" In Spanish, use the present: ¿Qué tal si vamos al cine? or ¿Y si vamos al cine?

Quedar: to meet up

Quedar is the magic verb for going out in Spain: ¿Quedamos? (shall we meet up?), ¿A qué hora quedamos?, ¿Dónde quedamos?, Quedamos en la plaza a las ocho. Quedar con alguien = to meet up with someone, to have plans with them: He quedado con Marta.

Una cita is a doctor's appointment or a romantic date. Between friends, you simply say quedar.

", "

Accepting and declining

To acceptTranslation
¡Vale!Okay!
¡Genial! / ¡Estupendo!Great! / Wonderful!
¡Me parece bien!Sounds good!
¡Buena idea!Good idea!
¡Claro que sí!Of course!
¡Me encantaría!I'd love to!
¡Venga, vamos!Come on, let's go!

Declining politely: always give an excuse

A blunt \"no\" is very rude in Spain. You apologize, give a reason, and often suggest something else. The essential little phrase: es que… (\"it's just that…\"), which introduces the excuse.

To declineTranslation
Lo siento, no puedo, es que tengo que trabajar.Sorry, I can't, it's just that I have to work.
¡Qué pena! Ese día no puedo.What a shame! I can't that day.
Me encantaría, pero estoy muy cansada.I'd love to, but I'm really tired.
Gracias, pero hoy no me apetece mucho.Thanks, but I don't really feel like it today.
Otro día será.Maybe another time.

Me encantaría, pero… is the most elegant way to say no: the conditional softens everything, just like \"I'd love to, but…\"

", "

Suggesting something else and setting the time

SentenceTranslation
¿Y si lo dejamos para el sábado?What if we put it off until Saturday?
¿Qué tal el domingo?How about Sunday?
¿Te viene bien el martes?Does Tuesday work for you?
Mejor otro día.Another day would be better.
¿Podríamos quedar un poco más tarde?Could we meet a little later?

Venir bien works like gustar: ¿Te viene bien? (does that work for you?), El jueves no me viene bien. Dejar para = to put off until: Lo dejamos para mañana.

Meeting up, Spanish style

You set the place and the time: Quedamos a las nueve en la puerta del cine (\"outside the movie theater\" is often en la puerta de). And don't forget Spanish hours: quedar a las diez para cenar is perfectly normal!

You can reuse the future and the conditional to confirm or give a heads-up:

Vale, allí estaré. Llegaré un poco tarde, es que salgo del trabajo a las ocho.Okay, I'll be there. I'll be a little late, it's just that I get off work at eight.
